rv.q: The work currently is caught in the middle between what a very famous actor might create as a performative work of autobiography and something more intensely focused on allowing viewers to see themselves in an archetypal journey.
What makes “Antonio’s Song” truly sing is its bone-authentic journey from the worst to the best of human nature.
This is powerful storytelling at its absolute finest and a dynamic celebration of the importance of art in all our lives.
Striking and enveloping, “Antonio’s Song/I Was Dreaming of my Son” is the most honest and accurate portrayal of how men are formed emotionally that I have ever seen.
Antonio's Song is a brilliant, moving, and virtuosic performance that captures the essence of his journey.
"Antonio’s Song/ I Was Dreaming of a Son” is an incredibly powerful meditation on identity.
Suarez is a fluid and compelling performer, mostly because he makes us feel that every step of his own story is still fresh in his own memory and etched into his flesh and bones.

cn.t: Critics praise this emotionally powerful autobiographical solo work, lauding Antonio Edwards Suarez's honest exploration of masculinity, fatherhood, and artistic identity, with Dael Orlandersmith's co-writing bringing authenticity and universal resonance.
